intro: Ivory Coast, officially Côte d'Ivoire, is the world's largest cocoa producer and one of West Africa's biggest economies.

chapters.title: Kingdoms
text: Before colonial rule, peoples such as the Akan, Senufo, Dan and Kru lived here. The Kong Empire in the north was a centre of Islamic learning and trade, and the Baoulé are said to have arrived after fleeing the Asante under Queen Pokou.

chapters.title: French colony
text: European traders named the coast after its ivory trade. France made it a colony in 1893, and Africans were forced to work on plantations and roads.

chapters.title: Independence and conflict
text: Félix Houphouët-Boigny led the country to independence in 1960 and ruled until 1993; cocoa and coffee brought a long boom called the 'Ivorian miracle'. He built a giant basilica in his home town, Yamoussoukro.
Civil wars in 2002 to 2007 and after the 2010 election split the country. Alassane Ouattara has been president since 2011.
